The bonds component is constructed to optimize stability and predictable cash flows, while taking into account the laddered maturity structure constraint. A 60% allocation is proposed for equities, which will be comprised of 40% high-quality large-cap stocks, primarily from developed markets, and 20% mid-cap and small-cap stocks. This allocation ensures exposure to various sectors and industries, minimizing concentration risks. 30% of the portfolio will be allocated to bonds, employing a 60/40 split between investment-grade corporate bonds and government bonds. This mix of corporate and government exposure provides a balance between credit and interest rate risks. 10% is allocated to commodities, primarily to gold and other precious metals, offering a hedge against inflation and market volatility. The bonds component is designed with a laddered maturity structure, ensuring that no more than 30% matures within any given year. This will result in a portfolio duration of approximately 6.5 years, which is within the approved credit quality and duration limits.
